reading: A small coloured shape sits outside a rectangular outline of 6. The shape is stretched to fill the outline's interior (its edge rows/columns run along the interior's edges) in its own colour, and the original shape is erased.

slots.subject: the small non-outline object (any colour, 2x2 or 1x1 box)
slots.target: interior of the rectangular outline object
slots.mapping: shape's box rescaled to the interior box: top/bottom rows and left/right columns of the shape map to the interior's edges; middle cells copy the edge pattern

why: the interior gets the subject's colour exactly where the stretched shape covers it; the outline is unchanged; the subject's original cells become background

reading: The 5x5 input is scaled up by a factor equal to the number of distinct non-background colours. Then diagonal lines of colour 2 are drawn outward from each corner of the scaled square object, through background, until the border or a coloured cell.

slots.scale: number of distinct non-zero colours in the input (3, 2, 4)
slots.diagonal_source: the four outer corners of the interior square object after scaling
slots.stop: grid border or first non-background cell

why: output = input with each cell blown up k x k (k = colour count), plus 2-diagonals from the square's corners covering only former background
invariants: colour layout of the input preserved at scale k

reading: Each single coloured cell sits at odd coordinates (2i+1, 2j+1) of a 10x10 grid; the output is 20x20 and each such cell becomes a 4x4 block at rows 4i..4i+3, cols 4j..4j+3.

slots.downsample: take cell (2i+1,2j+1) of each 2x2 block -> 5x5 grid
slots.upscale: each cell of the 5x5 grid becomes a 4x4 block -> 20x20

why: every 4x4 block of the output is uniform and equals input cell (2i+1,2j+1)

reading: A full-row and full-column separator of one colour splits the grid; the top-left quadrant holds a shape of another colour. The output is that quadrant recoloured to the separator colour and mirrored into a 4-fold symmetric grid of twice the quadrant size.

slots.unit: top-left panel cut by the cross separator
slots.colour: the separator colour replaces the shape colour
slots.layout: 2x2 arrangement: unit, horizontal flip, vertical flip, 180-degree rotation

why: output is symmetric about both its middle axes and its top-left quarter equals the top-left panel with fg recoloured to the separator colour

reading: The input's two colours are swapped (background and foreground exchange) and the result is tiled 2x2.
why: each of the four output blocks equals the input with colour 0 and its single foreground colour exchanged
invariants: only the two input colours appear

reading: An 8-shape fits in a 3x3 box; scattered single 4 cells are counted. The output is the shape's 3x3 box repeated horizontally once per 4 cell.

slots.unit: 3x3 box of the 8 object (padded to 3x3 when the shape is only 2 rows tall, empty row on top)
slots.layout: count copies side by side in one row

why: output is 3 x 3n with n = number of 4 markers, every 3x3 block equal to the shape box

reading: Vertical 8 bars have distinct lengths (plus many length-2 bars); one bar has half its cells (top or bottom half) coloured 9. That bar reverts to all 8, and the bar two cells longer gets the same half (top or bottom) coloured 9.
verb: pass marking to next longer bar

slots.source: the vertical segment containing 9 cells, length L
slots.target: the vertical segment of length L+2
slots.half: same end (top or bottom) as the 9 cells in the source; covers half the target's length

why: exactly the source's 9s become 8 and exactly half of the target bar (same end) becomes 9
invariants: all bar positions and lengths unchanged

reading: The 3x3 input is placed into a 9x9 grid at the block positions given by the cells of the input's least frequent colour; other blocks are empty (0).
why: block (i,j) of the output is the input iff input cell (i,j) has the colour with the fewest pixels, else all 0

reading: The coloured rows at the top are mirrored to the bottom so the grid becomes symmetric about its horizontal middle.
why: output is symmetric top-bottom about the grid's middle row axis; the top rows are unchanged

reading: A single off-colour cell in a uniform grid is expanded into the rectangle spanning from it to the nearest grid corner, filled with its colour.

new_rows.name: corner_box
new_rows.datalog:
hmax(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
wmax(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
rowin(R) :- cell(Y, X, C), hmax(H), D = H - Y, Y <= D, px(R, X2, C2), R <= Y.
rowin(R) :- cell(Y, X, C), hmax(H), D = H - Y, Y > D, px(R, X2, C2), R >= Y.
colin(K) :- cell(Y, X, C), wmax(W), D = W - X, X <= D, px(Y2, K, C2), K <= X.
colin(K) :- cell(Y, X, C), wmax(W), D = W - X, X > D, px(Y2, K, C2), K >= X.
corner_box(R, K) :- rowin(R), colin(K).

why: every cell of the box between the marker and the nearest grid corner takes the marker's colour; nothing else changes
